CVE-2026-102537.title: bacnet-stack BACnet/SC node always accepts a self-signed hub cert, so an attacker can MITM it
CVE-2026-102537.description: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, and 1.6.1, bws_cli_connect() in ports/linux/websocket-cli.c loads the trusted CA cert into the libwebsockets context, then always sets LCCSCF_ALLOW_SELFSIGNED in the connection flags. So lws accepts any self-signed hub certificate, whether or not it chains to the loaded CA. A BACnet/SC node finishes the TLS handshake to a rogue hub that presents a self-signed cert. It then hands the attacker its identity (VMAC, UUID) and all later BACnet traffic. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.

CVE-2026-104100.title: Teable: Arbitrary root file write via attachment presign hash path traversal
CVE-2026-104100.description: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

CVE-2026-126360.title: OpenTelemetry Python: Denial of service through quadratic-time traceparent parsing in opentelemetry-api
CVE-2026-126360.description: OpenTelemetry Python provides the Python API and SDK for OpenTelemetry. Prior to 1.45.2, TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract() in opentelemetry-api can perform quadratic-time regular-expression backtracking on a malformed traceparent value containing a trace-context prefix, a long whitespace sequence, and an embedded newline. Exploitation requires an attacker-controlled carrier that preserves embedded newlines and permits a sufficiently large value, because conforming HTTP header values cannot contain embedded newlines. JSON-based carriers, including applicable MCP request metadata integrations, can preserve the required newline depending on the SDK, instrumentation, and message-size limits. Parsing on an asynchronous server's event-loop thread can consume excessive CPU and delay unrelated requests, while the advisory does not establish disclosure, modification, or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.45.2.

When generating attachment thumbnails or rendering event graph preview images, the application decodes user-supplied image data using the GD library without first validating the declared pixel dimensions in the image header.

- An authenticated MISP user with permission to upload attachments or to create/view event graphs.
- The ability to supply a crafted image file (e.g., a PNG with a valid header declaring oversized dimensions).

CVE-2026-87027.title: TDE temporary-file encryption key incompletely initialized in EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server
CVE-2026-87027.description: In EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server versions 15 through 18 with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled, the key used to encrypt temporary files was incompletely initialized. The code applied sizeof() to a pointer to the key buffer rather than to the buffer itself, so only 8 of the intended 32 bytes were filled from a secure random source and the remaining 24 bytes kept whatever was already in memory. This reduces the guaranteed randomness of the temporary-file key from 256 bits to 64 bits. Exploiting this requires local read access to the server's temporary-file directory, and those files normally exist only while the server is running; they persist only after a crash and are removed at the next server start. Permanent data files and WAL are not affected. The issue is fixed in EDB Postgres Extended Server 15.20, 16.16, 17.12 and 18.7 and EDB Postgres Advanced Server 15.20.0, 16.16.0, 17.12.0 and 18.7.0; the server must be restarted after upgrading.

CVE-2026-99446.title: phy: core: Fix race-condition between _of_phy_get() and try_module_get()
CVE-2026-99446.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

phy: core: Fix race-condition between _of_phy_get() and try_module_get()

Sashiko asked during a patch review if the existing usage pattern had a
race condition; specifically in of_phy_get() if it was possible between
returning from _of_phy_get() and running try_module_get() that a module
might be unbound leading to use-after-free.

Looking at the code this appears to be so, there is no linkage between the
phy and module under a synchronisation primitive.

Using the phy_provider_mutex in phy_get() will ensure there is a link between
the returned phy pointer and the module_get() bumping the module reference
count.

Amend phy_get(), of_phy_get() and devm_of_phy_get_by_index() to fix the
same usage pattern.

phy_provider_unregister() must take the phy_provider_mutex so amending
phy_get()/of_phy_get() to take that same mutex guarantees there is no
use-after-free.

CVE-2026-99622.title: drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails
CVE-2026-99622.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails

import_obj_create() takes a reference on the dma-buf for the new kgd_mem,
but the error path after validating the BO doesn't drop it. Since the
validation reserves the BO interruptibly, an import failing with
-ERESTARTSYS leaks the exported BO with its memory, and keeps the module
in use.

Importing a 64 MiB VRAM BO in a loop while getting SIGUSR1
every 20 us and another thread changes the BO's mappings:

INFO: 171821 imports, VRAM used before 65 MiB, after 129 MiB
modprobe: FATAL: Module amdgpu is in use.

Drop the reference, and free the sync object and the mutex of the kgd_mem
as well. With that VRAM usage returns to 65 MiB after the same test.

(cherry picked from commit b4d1eca2729840148ff2ea957724ce764ca5a94e)

CVE-2026-99657.title: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab()
CVE-2026-99657.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab()

Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call
mmu_interval_notifier_remove() when freeing a buffer object.
__mmu_interval_notifier_insert() sets ->mm before validating the range,
so a wrapping userptr range can leave ->mm set after insertion fails.
Cleanup then tries to remove an unregistered notifier for which no mm
reference was acquired.

Set ->mm only after mmgrab(), once insertion can no longer fail. While
we could fix radeon's code instead, setting ->mm on success only makes
the code more robust.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.
